title: The search
hook: monkeys sent in four directions; Sampati the vulture's news

segments.voice: Last time: chaturmas, four months of rain and a hero who couldn't move. Waiting is a season.

A lost set of keys. The whole house turned upside down. Then a grandmother, without getting up from her chair, asks: did you check your coat? Hold on to that. The rains end, and Sugriva, now king and comfortable, has half forgotten his promise. Lakshmana storms into the monkey city so angry the walls seem to shake, and it takes Tara, the wise queen, to calm him down. Then Sugriva moves fast. He sends his whole army out in four great search parties: north, east, west and south. One month, he says. Search every mountain, every forest, every cave. And he gives Hanuman, heading south, Rama's ring.
screen: `THE RAINS END.` → `LAKSHMANA STORMS IN.` → `FOUR ARMIES, FOUR DIRECTIONS.` → `HANUMAN GETS THE RING.`

segments.voice: The northern, eastern and western parties come home with nothing. The southern party, with Hanuman and young Angada, Vali's son, finds nothing either. They get lost in an enchanted cave. The month runs out. They sit down on the shore of the ocean, at the very tip of the land, and give up. Going home empty-handed feels impossible, so, in Valmiki's telling, they decide to fast there until they die. As they talk, Angada mentions Jatayu, the old bird who died fighting Ravana. And a voice answers from the cliffs. An enormous, ancient vulture with no wings has heard the name. It's Sampati, Jatayu's older brother. Long ago, he says, the two brothers raced toward the sun, and when Jatayu flew too close, Sampati spread his wings over him, and his own wings burned away. He's been stuck on this cliff ever since, and he hadn't heard his brother was dead until now. Then Sampati gives them what a whole army couldn't find. A vulture's eyes see very far, he says. I can see her. Across the ocean, a hundred yojanas away, in the city of Lanka, sits Sita. And as he speaks, in the story, new wings begin to grow. Notice where the answer came from. Not from running harder, but from an old, broken bird on a cliff, the one nobody thought to ask, and because someone spoke with love about his brother. His news sends Hanuman to the ocean's edge, and to the great leap you already know.
screen: `THE MONTH RUNS OUT.` · `A VOICE FROM THE CLIFF: SAMPATI.` · `HE BURNED HIS WINGS FOR HIS BROTHER.` · `I CAN SEE HER: LANKA.`

segments.voice: Think of something you've been searching for, an answer, a direction, a way through, and notice where you've been looking: online, round and round in your own head, the same three friends. Then ask: who's the old bird I haven't asked? A grandparent, a retired neighbor, someone who's been through it, someone you've written off; let a face come up, and just notice who you've been walking past.
The search. An army in four directions, a month gone, and the answer from a wingless old bird on a cliff.
Your line: ask the old bird. The answer came from the last place anyone looked. Day fifty-seven.

howItsDone: The search for Sita and Sampati's news are told in Ramayana readings and recitations; the scene leads straight into the Sundara Kanda, Hanuman's leap to Lanka, which is often recited on its own.

original.note: Sanskrit: Sampati, the old vulture, elder brother of Jatayu.

trapdoor: what you thought: the monkeys searched until they found her.
what it means: they failed, gave up, and the answer came from an old wingless bird nobody thought to ask.
what a scholar hears: in Valmiki, Sampati's wings grow back as he helps, and his news turns the story to the Sundara Kanda, Hanuman's leap.

notes: Sampati's account of shielding Jatayu from the sun, the distance of a hundred yojanas, and his wings regrowing follow Valmiki as remembered; please confirm.
The enchanted cave (Svayamprabha's cave) is mentioned without its name; confirm.
The southern party's decision to fast to death (prayopavesha) is described plainly; confirm the framing is appropriate.
